literal: Any matter whatsoever they will not pry into, they will not pursue; but when that matter is disclosed, let them listen to the secret.
translation: Those who associate with rulers should never pry into any of their affairs, nor pursue them with questions; but when the ruler himself chooses to disclose a secret, they may listen to it.
modern: அரசரோடு பழகுகின்றவர்கள் எந்த ஒரு விஷயத்தையும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்க மாட்டார்கள்; அதனைத் தொடர்ந்து கேட்கவும் மாட்டார்கள். ஆனால், அரசர் அந்த ரகசியத்தை அவராகவே வெளியிடும்போது மட்டும் அதனைக் கேட்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet advises courtiers on how to handle confidential matters in the presence of a ruler. A wise associate does not pry into the ruler's affairs or ask probing questions to uncover secrets. They must show restraint and not pursue matters that are not voluntarily shared. However, if the ruler chooses to disclose a secret on their own accord, the associate may then listen to it. The key words 'ஓரார்' (will not pry) and 'தொடரார்' (will not pursue) emphasize the strict boundaries of curiosity one must maintain around authority.
